title: CLR/39/2012 of SMT RASHMI SHARMA Vs DR. SMT SUDESH PRABHA BASSI and ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
MCC No. 618 of 2013
With
CLMA No. 10666 of 2013
IN
Civil Revision No. 39 of 2012
Smt. Rashmi Sharma Ö..Defendant/Revisionist
Versus
Dr. Smt. Sudesh Prabha Bassi and another
 ......Ö.Plaintiff/Opposite Party
Present:
Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, Advocate for the revisionist/applicant.
Mr. D. Barthwal, Advocate for the plaintiff/respondents.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Vide order dated 5.12.2012, tenant/revisionist
was directed to deposit entire decreetal amount with the
learned J.S.C.C. within a period of three months and to
continue to deposit an amount of `15,000/- per month
towards mesne profit as awarded by learned J.S.C.C. It
was further directed that on deposit of decreetal amount,
tenant/revisionist shall not be evicted. However, interim
order dated 5.12.2012 was not complied with and no
deposit was made within the time stipulated by this
Court.
Vide order dated 2.4.2013, ten daysí more time
was granted to the revisionist/tenant to make compliance
of the interim order dated 5.12.2012.
When revision was taken up for hearing on
7.5.2013, none was present for the tenant/revisionist.
Mr. D. Barthwal, learned counsel for the
landlord/respondents informed this Court that interim
order dated 5.12.2012 was not complied with. Having

2
recorded so, this Court vacated interim order giving
liberty to the executing court to proceed with the
execution of the decree and revision was directed to be
listed for 27.5.2013 in the interest of justice.
None was present on 27.5.2013, therefore, this
Court was pleased to dismiss the revision vide order
dated 27.5.2013.
Now present application has been moved by
the tenant/revisionist to review/recall the order dated
27.5.2013, whereby revision filed by the
revisionist/tenant was dismissed.
I have heard Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned
counsel for the revisionist/tenant and Mr. D. Barthwal,
learned counsel for the landlord/respondents.
Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel for the
revisionist/applicant submits that this Court has erred
in dismissing the revision petition on merit in the
absence of counsel for the revisionist and this Court
should have dismissed the revision only for non-prosecution.
I have carefully perused the order dated
25.7.2013. In view of the fact that none was present for
the revisionist on 25.7.2013, revision shall be deemed to
have been dismissed for non-prosecution in the absence
of counsel for the revisionist. Merely because this Court
observed that impugned order did not suffer any
illegality, does not mean that revision shall be deemed to
have been dismissed on merit.
In view of provisions of Order 41 Rule 19 CPC,
appeal or revision, even if dismissed on merit in the
absence of counsel for the appellant or revisionist, as the

3
case may be, shall be deemed to have been dismissed for
non-prosecution.
Now question arises as to whether order dated
25.7.2013 should be recalled restoring the petition at its
original number and an opportunity should be granted to
the applicant/revisionist to argue the writ petition.
In view of the findings recorded hereinbefore,
despite several opportunities granted, revisionist did not
make compliance of the interim order and did not deposit
decreetal amount and mesne profit. Not only this, no
attempt was made to seek permission from this Court to
deposit the decreetal amount and the amount of mesne
profit during the pendency of present application.
Therefore, it seems that tenant/revisionist is not coming
before this Court with clean hands. Hence, applying the
principle that he who seeks equity must come with clean
hands, I am not inclined to restore revision.
Applications, MCC No. 618 of 2013 and CLMA
No. 10666/2013 are being dismissed.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 1.3.2014
Avneet
